get.description:
The applications one published link produced, newest first.

**Why this route exists rather than a flag on the operator queue.** A POS
case is born ``awaiting_verification``, which ``CaseRepo.list_cases``
excludes by default (``HIDDEN_FROM_QUEUE_STATES``) because an applicant who
has not proved control of their address is not queue work. That default is
left exactly as it is: this route reads ``CaseRepo.list_by_origin``, a
separate query whose whole purpose is those rows. Widening ``GET /api/cases``
with an ``exclude_states`` parameter would have moved the hidden-state
decision into a client argument and changed the queue's contract for every
caller; the counting reads (``count_in_flight`` for billing,
``count_for_admission`` for the door) are untouched either way — neither
reads this route or its repo method.

Scoped twice, deliberately: ``get_for_tenant`` proves the portal is the
caller's (404 rather than 403 for another tenant's id, matching
``update_pos_portal`` so this route cannot be used to probe which ids
exist), and ``list_by_origin`` puts ``tenant_id`` in the WHERE clause as
well. Isolation does not rest on one check.

Parties come back with the case because that is what the resend action is
addressed by — ``POST /api/cases/{case_id}/portal/parties/{party_id}/
resend-code``. The access code is NOT here and is not derivable from
anything here; the operator can command a re-send to the address on file and
nothing more.

post.description:
Regenerate a party's 5-digit access code (and reset the attempt counter).

A borrower who fumbled the code 5 times is locked out, or the operator just
wants a fresh code to share. Mints a NEW random 5-digit code on the active
token and clears attempts — the link (token) is unchanged, only the code the
borrower types. Returns the new code so the operator can read it out.

schema.title: Response Reissue Link Api Cases  Case Id  Portal Parties  Party Id  Reissue Post

post.description:
Re-send the borrower's existing 5-digit access code to their own address.

The stuck-borrower remedy: a POS applicant whose first email never arrived
has an application nobody can reach, because the code lives only in
``portal_tokens.access_code``.

**Resend, never reveal.** The code is not in the response, not in the log,
and not derivable from either — see ``ResendCodeResponse``. Nor can the
operator supply or change the destination: there is deliberately NO request
body, so the address is whatever ``portal_parties.email`` already holds, and
the refusal in ``code_email._recipient_was_substituted`` still applies —
an address written through the borrower's own link after party creation is
refused here exactly as it is for the borrower's ``request_code`` intent.
Without that, this route would be the bypass that rule exists to prevent.

Sibling comparison, because it is easy to misread this route as stricter
than it is: ``reissue_link`` above MINTS a new code and returns it to the
operator, by design and unchanged. What is guarded here is the resend of the
EXISTING code — the one an unverified borrower may already hold — not the
operator's ability to hand out a fresh one.

Every refusal is a status code, never a 200 with a sad sentence: an operator
resending into a reaped case must not read like a success.

delete.description: Remove a party (and its thread) from a case's portal.

Operator soft-deletes one of their OWN messages from a party's thread.

Own-only: the operator may delete ONLY operator-authored messages — never a
borrower's message. Guarded against IDOR: case access is verified, the
message must exist, belong to the URL party, and that party must belong to
the URL case. Upload bubbles are synthesized from events (non-row ids), so
``get_message`` returns None for them — they 404 here and stay undeletable.
The delete is SOFT (``deleted_at`` set, row kept) so the thread shows a
tombstone. After delete, publishes ``portal.thread_changed`` so both sides
refetch.

patch.description:
Operator edits the body of one of their OWN messages on a party's thread.

Own-only: only operator-authored messages may be edited — never a borrower's.
Guarded against IDOR: case access is verified, the message must exist, belong
to the URL party, and that party must belong to the URL case. A deleted
message can't be edited (404 — its content is gone). An empty/whitespace body
is rejected (422). After the edit, publishes ``portal.thread_changed`` so
both sides refetch.

schema.title: Response Get Events Api Cases  Case Id  Events Get

get.description:
SSE stream of case events. Polls Postgres by event_id cursor.

Clients connect and receive events as they arrive:
    data: {"event_id": 1, "event_type": "qualify.spec.evaluated", ...}

Pass ``?cursor=N`` to start from event_id N+1 (exclusive). The client
should backfill historical events via ``GET /events`` first, record the
last event_id, then open this stream with ``?cursor=<last_id>``. This
prevents the stream from replaying historical ``case.system.completed``
events on every reconnect — which would cause an immediate ``stream.end``
even though the case is still receiving refinement events.

get.summary: Get the signed attestation artifact for a case
get.description:
Return the case's Signed Tree Head as a signed in-toto attestation.

The artifact carries the in-toto Statement (subject = source documents,
predicate = the Merkle Signed Tree Head), a detached signature, the schema
catalog, a compact JWS for offline verification, and the issuer public JWK.

Pass ``?format=jws`` to receive only ``{"jws": "<compact-jws>"}`` — useful
for clients that verify the JWS directly without the expanded artifact.

Errors: 409 when the case is not finalized, 422 when its audit log is empty,
404 when the case does not exist, 404/403 when the caller may not access it.

schema.description: When 'jws', return only the compact JWS as {"jws": ...}.

parameters.description: When 'jws', return only the compact JWS as {"jws": ...}.

409.description: Case is not finalized; no attestation can be issued yet.

422.description: Case has an empty audit log; nothing to attest.

get.summary: Get a Merkle inclusion proof for one audit event
get.description:
Return a Merkle inclusion (audit) proof that ``event_id`` is in the tree.

The proof's ``leaf`` is the base64url-encoded canonical leaf payload bytes
(the exact bytes that were hashed); clients re-hash it and walk
``audit_path`` to reconstruct ``merkle_root``.

Errors: 404 when the case or the event does not exist, 409 when the case is
not finalized, 422 when its audit log is empty.

200.description: Inclusion proof reconstructing the signed Merkle root.

409.description: Case is not finalized; no signed tree to prove against.

422.description: Case has an empty audit log.

get.summary: Get a Merkle consistency proof between two tree sizes
get.description:
Return a Merkle consistency proof between sizes ``from`` and ``to``.

Proves the audit log at the smaller size is an untampered prefix of the log
at the larger size — the append-only guarantee. Both roots are returned so
a verifier can confirm each independently.

Errors: 400 for an invalid range (require ``1 <= from <= to <= tree_size``),
404 when the case does not exist, 409 when the case is not finalized.

parameters.name: to

schema.description: Later (larger or equal) tree size; must be >= from.
schema.title: To

parameters.description: Later (larger or equal) tree size; must be >= from.

200.description: Consistency proof that the first tree is a prefix of the second.

422.description: Case has an empty audit log.

get.description:
List the caller's tenant-scoped loan products.

Returns the full ``TenantProductView`` for each row in
``tenant_products`` (or the YAML fallback when the tenant hasn't been
seeded yet — see ``policy.product_registry.list_tenant_products``).
The shape is rich enough for Lux to render the approach + product
pickers without a separate config endpoint.

``initial_required_inputs`` is folded in per row so the Create Case
modal can render its dynamic form straight from this fetch (no
second round-trip). Each row's schema comes from
``initial_required_inputs_schema`` which is DB-first
(``spec_versions`` + ``product_specs`` join, with a YAML fallback
for unseeded dev DBs). The wire shape is a flat
``list[UserInputFieldResponse]`` — every entry on this list is
already scoped to a single product, so the groups+products wrapper
used by the refine endpoint would degenerate to a single mirror
entry. Products without any ``required_at_create`` inputs return
``[]`` so the frontend can do a uniform ``fields.length === 0``
check.

different payloads. The typed fields are the cross-cutting ones the UI
reads: the ``_agent`` meta, the ``_display`` render-ready block, the
correction op (``field``/``old_value``/``new_value``,
``reason``/``score_basis``/``reasoning``), the severity badge, and a
free-text ``message``.

CreatePosPortalRequest.title: CreatePosPortalRequest
CreatePosPortalRequest.description:
What an LO chooses. The slug is NOT one of those things.

A client-supplied slug would be a land grab on a global namespace and a
second place for URL-safety to go wrong; the server mints it.

CreateTenantRequest.title: CreateTenantRequest
CreateTenantRequest.description: Body for POST /auth/create-tenant — authenticated user self-registers a tenant.

CurePlanItem.title: CurePlanItem
CurePlanItem.description:
One stretch-lever cure option for a marginal DSCR file (framework §6.7 / D5).

The DECISION of which levers cure a file lives entirely in the DSCR spec
YAML (``lever_*_cures`` flags + ``DSCR_CURE_*`` findings carrying the
human-readable sentences). This is the first-class, typed projection of the
structured list that ``qualify.evaluation._build_cure_plan`` assembles into
``spec_results.derivations`` — it carries numbers only, never display
strings (labels/sentences come from the spec/config + findings, per the
"display strings from data, not code" rule). ``lever`` is the stable id the
UI/config keys cure labels on (``"down_payment"`` / ``"interest_only"`` /
``"market_rent"``).

Fields are nullable because each lever populates a different subset:

  * ``down_payment``: ``additional_down`` + ``cured_ltv``
    (``resulting_dscr`` == ``target_dscr`` by construction).
  * ``interest_only``: ``io_dscr`` (== ``resulting_dscr``).
  * ``market_rent``: ``market_rent`` + ``market_dscr`` (== ``resulting_dscr``).

``extra = "allow"`` forward-compats new levers (C/D/F) that add numeric keys
without forcing a types.py change.

DraftRequestBody.title: DraftRequestBody
DraftRequestBody.description: Draft-only — turns selected items into borrower-friendly text.

EditMessageBody.title: EditMessageBody
EditMessageBody.description: Operator edits the body of one of their OWN thread messages.

EventDisplay.title: EventDisplay
EventDisplay.description:
Server-driven, render-ready view of a correction-agent event.

Built at the emit boundary (``domains.corrections.display.build_display``)
so consumers render the audit event generically: a narrative ``summary``
(the agent's own note with opaque refs resolved to names), humanized
``fields``, correction ``ops`` as cards, and the ``documents`` it references
as clickable viewer links. No client-side humanization, ref/id resolution,
or domain vocabulary required.

EventDisplayDoc.title: EventDisplayDoc
EventDisplayDoc.description:
A document this event references, as a clickable link into the viewer.

``file_id`` + ``page`` are what the host needs to open the document viewer
(``/case/{id}/view?file=&page=``); ``label`` is the human caption
(``W-2 p.1``) and ``doc_type`` lets the host route bank statements, etc.

EventDisplayField.title: EventDisplayField
EventDisplayField.description:
One render-ready label/value row in an event's ``_display`` block.

``value`` is already humanized server-side (refs resolved to names, doc-ids
to ``W-2 p.1`` labels, snake_case to words); it may be a scalar, a list, or
a nested object — the consumer renders it structurally without interpreting.

EventDisplayOp.title: EventDisplayOp
EventDisplayOp.description: One gated correction op, rendered as a card.

EventDisplayOpChange.title: EventDisplayOpChange
EventDisplayOpChange.description: A before→after value change on a correction op (humanized).

ExtractionSourceRef.title: ExtractionSourceRef
ExtractionSourceRef.description:
Page + bbox provenance carried alongside an input extraction.

``file_id`` is the underlying file UUID — hosts wire this into their
document viewer's ``?file=…&page=…`` deep-link convention (page_number is
1-based, matching ``pages.page_number``).

HeadlineMetric.title: HeadlineMetric
HeadlineMetric.description:
Big-number headline rendered above the scenario page metadata.

Populated when the active loan product declares a
``summary.headline_metric`` block in ``loan_products.yaml`` (DSCR uses
this to surface the DSCR ratio in place of the default
``$X,XXX/mo`` total_monthly_income chip). ``value`` is the
pre-formatted display string (e.g. ``"2.65x"``); the UI renders it
verbatim with ``label`` as the tooltip / accessibility text so
operators see which metric drove the headline.

IdentityInfo.description: Unified case-identity read model. Discriminator field: kind.

IdentityRef.title: IdentityRef
IdentityRef.description: Lightweight reference to one end of a relationship.

InclusionProofResponse.description: Merkle inclusion (audit) proof that one event is in the signed tree.

InputProvenance.description:
Single contributing extraction for a derivation input.

`value` is the engine-side normalized value the derivation actually
saw; `raw_value` is the unparsed text the extraction stored. Together
with `doc_id` + `canonical_key` they let the UI render
``W2.wages_y1 → $5,000`` chips that click through to a specific
page/bbox.

InputValueResponse.title: InputValueResponse
InputValueResponse.description: One variable that fed a derivation step, with all contributing extractions.

IntegrationRegisterRequest.description:
Self-serve registration for any push provider (resolved from the
registry). Creates a tenant + API credential and hands ``params`` to the
provider's own register handler — the endpoint hardcodes no provider.

``params`` carries provider-specific fields, e.g. for Brook:
``{sf_instance_url, sf_webhook_url, sf_webhook_secret}``.

JoinTenantRequest.description: Body for POST /auth/tenant/join — user redeems a tenant invite code.

A knowledge-based-auth question derived from the case's identity facts.

Only the prompt is sent — never the expected answer. The borrower's answer
is checked server-side (see veritas.domains.identity.kba).

MyCaseLink.title: MyCaseLink
MyCaseLink.description: A case the signed-in borrower can access, plus a fresh portal token.

OfficerAvatarUpdate.description: Set (or clear, with null) the firm's loan-officer profile photo.

OfficerProfile.description: The firm's loan-officer profile, as shown in the chat avatar.

PartyDocument.description: A document this party is related to, and their role on it.

PartyFact.title: PartyFact
PartyFact.description: A small grounded label/value pair (employer, DOB, ...).

PartyIdentifier.title: PartyIdentifier
PartyIdentifier.description:
A masked government identifier — tail only, never the full value.

``type`` is the kind of identifier the linked person/entity carries
(``ssn`` | ``itin`` | ``ein`` | ...); ``last4`` is the only recoverable
portion. Both are ``None`` when the party has no linked identity or the
identifier was never captured.

PartyMention.title: PartyMention
PartyMention.description:
A document this party appears on, and their role on it.

``file_id``/``page``/``bbox`` locate the appearance so the operator UI can
deep-link into the document viewer (``?file=&page=&bbox=``). All three are
best-effort: a mention with no resolvable source still carries doc_id, label
and role. ``bbox`` is a normalized ``{x, y, width, height}`` (0-1 fractions)
when the source record exposes one, else ``None``.

PartyProfile.title: PartyProfile
PartyProfile.description:
Operator profile for a single party.

Every enrichment beyond the basics (name/role/status/documents) is
best-effort: a party with no linked identity, or whose documents carry no
facts, still returns a valid profile with empty contact/identifier fields.

PartyStatus.title: PartyStatus
PartyStatus.description: The party-scoped lifecycle flags already computed for the overview.

PartyUploadedDocument.title: PartyUploadedDocument
PartyUploadedDocument.description: A document uploaded through this party's portal chat.

PortalDocumentRequirement.title: PortalDocumentRequirement
PortalDocumentRequirement.description:
One row of the product's borrower-facing document ask list.

Every string comes from the product's ``required_documents`` block in
``policy/specs/loan_products.yaml`` — the list that answers "what is the
applicant ASKED to upload", which is NOT the calculation spec's
``activation.required_documents`` (that is the qualification gate, is
transaction-type-blind by design, and deliberately omits documents a
purchase case would never have). Nothing here is composed in Python.

``label`` is the row's borrower copy, falling back to the document type when
the YAML declares none. ``note`` is the optional second line ("If the
property is vacant you can skip this — …") and is ``""`` when unset.

``optional`` marks a row the applicant may skip. It is renderer metadata:
the server does not treat an optional row differently anywhere.

An ``any_of`` group ("a lease OR an STR revenue statement") is ONE row —
one upload satisfies it — so the count of rows is the count of asks, not the
count of document types.

PortalInputField.title: PortalInputField
PortalInputField.description:
One create-time input the applicant still has to answer.

Labels, units, bounds, options and ``required_when`` all come from the
product's own definition, so this renders generically — nothing
product-specific is encoded in the shape.

``default`` is often ``null``, and a client must not substitute one of its
own: some inputs are defaulted server-side, and pre-selecting a value
silently changes the answer the applicant gives.

PortalInputFieldOption.title: PortalInputFieldOption
PortalInputFieldOption.description:
One choice of an enum-typed spec input, as declared in the spec's
``override.options``. ``value`` is stringified because it is what the client
sends back and what the enum check compares.

PortalLinkRequest.title: PortalLinkRequest
PortalLinkRequest.description: Operator's request payload when generating a borrower portal link.

PortalLinkResponse.title: PortalLinkResponse
PortalLinkResponse.description:
A freshly issued borrower portal token for a case.

Veritas stays URL-agnostic (per design): it returns the token + expiry; the
client builds the shareable link (``<app>/portal?token=<token>``). Single-use,
time-limited (default 48h); no borrower login required.

PortalLinkStatusResponse.title: PortalLinkStatusResponse
PortalLinkStatusResponse.description:
Operator-facing status of a case's borrower portal link.

``status``: ``none`` (never issued), ``waiting`` (issued, borrower hasn't
submitted), ``submitted`` (borrower finished — link consumed).

PortalRequestItem.title: PortalRequestItem
PortalRequestItem.description:
One requested document/follow-up item the borrower will see.

``source`` records where it came from: ``follow_up`` / ``completeness`` (a
veritas-suggested item the operator checked off) or ``custom`` (free-typed).

PortalTokenRequest.title: PortalTokenRequest
PortalTokenRequest.description:
Request a borrower portal token for a case (tenant/operator only).

Used by external apps (e.g. the Brook Salesforce package) to invite a
borrower to upload documents before any have been processed.

PortalTokenResponse.title: PortalTokenResponse
PortalTokenResponse.description: A minted portal token + the Veritas-hosted borrower upload URL.

PosPortalCaseResponse.title: PosPortalCaseResponse
PosPortalCaseResponse.description:
One application started from a published link.

``name`` is ``None`` until the case reaches scenario naming (Task 1(a)
closed on that being the honest pre-qualification state), and ``state`` is
the raw case state — ``awaiting_verification`` for a borrower who has not
entered their code yet. Both are passed through unmapped: this module has no
business owning operator-facing wording for either.

PosPortalPartyResponse.title: PosPortalPartyResponse
PosPortalPartyResponse.description:
One person on a POS application, as the manage-links surface sees them.

Carries the ``party_id`` the resend route is addressed by and the address
the code would go to — and deliberately nothing that could substitute for
the access code. ``display_name`` is ``None`` for an applicant who has only
ever typed an email into a public form, which is every unverified POS
borrower; the client renders the address as their identity rather than
inventing a placeholder name.

url.title: Url
url.description: The public application URL to publish.

ProductResponse.title: ProductResponse
ProductResponse.description:
Tenant-scoped loan product configuration.

Returned by ``GET /products`` (a tenant's own catalog) and consumed by
Lux to drive ``<ApproachPicker>`` / ``<ProductPicker>`` data-driven.
The shape mirrors ``policy.product_registry.TenantProductView`` —
every field that matters for runtime resolution + UI rendering, so
the host never has to consult any other endpoint to render an
accurate picker.

``initial_required_inputs`` carries the operator-supplied schema for
fields flagged ``required_at_create: true`` on any of the product's
specs. The Create Case modal renders this directly via
``<DynamicUserInputsFormFields>`` and blocks submission until every
listed field has a valid value — single round-trip, no separate
schema endpoint. An empty list means the product has no must-know-
upfront values; the modal can skip rendering the form altogether.

ProductSuggestionItem.title: ProductSuggestionItem
ProductSuggestionItem.description: One ranked product suggestion with score breakdown.

RegenerateSuggestionsBody.title: RegenerateSuggestionsBody
RegenerateSuggestionsBody.description:
On-demand fresh suggestion generation for the composer.

``note`` is the operator's free-text ask (MUST appear as an item); ``exclude``
is the already-shown titles to avoid repeating ('generate more').

RelationshipInfo.title: RelationshipInfo
RelationshipInfo.description: One directed edge in the case relationship graph.

RenderingHints.title: RenderingHints
RenderingHints.description:
UI rendering decisions resolved server-side from scenario + manifest data.

Computed once by Veritas so every consumer (React, Vue, agents) gets
identical behavior without re-implementing detection logic locally.

ReportCatalogResponse.title: ReportCatalogResponse
ReportCatalogResponse.description:
Response from GET /cases/{case_id}/reports.

``income_report_name`` is the resolved income report for the scenario's
products — callers should use this instead of guessing from product IDs,
because product data may not be loaded yet when the UI renders.

``credit_available`` is true when the case has at least one uploaded
credit report document (CreditReport, SoftPullCreditReport, or
HardPullCreditReport). Used by the export modal to enable Credit/DTI
checkboxes without relying on a previously-generated credit report.

ReportGenerateResponse.title: ReportGenerateResponse
ReportGenerateResponse.description:
Returned after a report is rendered and stored.

report_id is None when no manifest was available to attach the Report row
to (e.g. a case-level report generated without a scenario).  Clients should
treat a null report_id as "rendered but not persisted for future retrieval".

ReportListItem.title: ReportListItem
ReportListItem.description: One entry in the GET /cases/{case_id}/reports list.

RequiredWhenConditionResponse.title: RequiredWhenConditionResponse
RequiredWhenConditionResponse.description:
Conditional-requirement predicate for an operator input.

The field is required ONLY when sibling input ``field`` equals
``equals``. Lets a spec express "Purchase Price is required when
transaction_type == purchase" without forcing it on refis. Read by
the create-case modal (lux ``validateInitialRequiredInputs``) and the
spec-engine pre-eval gate (``_validate_inputs_pre_eval``), which both
treat the field as required only when the predicate holds against the
current input values.

ResendCodeResponse.title: ResendCodeResponse
ResendCodeResponse.description:
Result of an operator-commanded access-code resend.

Carries NO code and NO address. The 5-digit access code is an
authentication factor — it proves the holder of the link controls the email
address — so an operator who could read it here could verify as the
borrower, and ``identity.borrower.verified`` would attest to something that
did not happen. ``detail`` is a sentence for the operator, so it must never
be built from either value.

SendRequestBody.title: SendRequestBody
SendRequestBody.description: Append a request to a party's portal thread.

merkle_root.title: Merkle Root
merkle_root.description: Hex-encoded Merkle root over all audit-log leaves.

tree_size.title: Tree Size
tree_size.description: Number of audit events covered by this tree head.

last_event_hash.title: Last Event Hash
last_event_hash.description: Hash chain value of the last event in the tree.

schema_catalog_hash.title: Schema Catalog Hash
schema_catalog_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical schema catalog for the covered events.

computations_root.title: Computations Root
computations_root.description: Hex Merkle root over the case's spec_results computation commitments.

provenance_root.title: Provenance Root
provenance_root.description: Hex Merkle root over the case's extraction-lineage records.

provenance_count.title: Provenance Count
provenance_count.description: Number of extraction-lineage records under provenance_root.

issuer.title: Issuer
issuer.description: Issuer block: name, tenant_id, environment, software_version.

SignedTreeHeadPredicate.title: SignedTreeHeadPredicate
SignedTreeHeadPredicate.description: The in-toto predicate body: the Signed Tree Head over a case's audit log.

SpecSummaryResultResponse.title: SpecSummaryResultResponse
SpecSummaryResultResponse.description:
Aggregated headline result derived from a set of ``SpecResultResponse`` rows.

Veritas computes one of these for every entity that holds spec results
(scenarios, refinements, future entities). The same shape carries any
policy domain — income, asset verification, DTI, reserves, etc. — so
consumers never special-case on "income".

The ``strategy`` field names the aggregation rule. For now the only
implemented rule is ``max_value``: bucket eligible results by spec-name
prefix, sum within each bucket, return the max bucket total. Additional
strategies (sum across buckets, weighted average, percentile, …) can be
introduced later as a backwards-compatible widening of the enum.

StatusResponse.title: StatusResponse
StatusResponse.description:
Live collection state for the borrower upload page poll (token-gated).

``reason`` is exactly the borrower-facing set — the secret-key ``/exchange``
path owns the separate ``pending_borrower`` nudge; it never surfaces here.

StructuredDocument.title: StructuredDocument
StructuredDocument.description:
One document's extractions grouped into ontology regions.

``regions`` maps region_id → value:
  static          → dict[str, Any]   (canonical_key suffix → raw value)
  table/adaptive  → list[dict]       (one dict per extracted row)

SuggestedProductsResponse.title: SuggestedProductsResponse
SuggestedProductsResponse.description:
Document-driven product suggestion for a case.

Computed by the post-stitch hook (see
``temporal.activities.stitch.stitch_activity``) and persisted on
``cases.suggested_product_ids``. The ``case.products.suggested`` SSE
event carries the same payload so the UI can live-update without
polling.

``suggested_product_ids`` is empty (and ``computed_at`` ``None``)
when stitch hasn't run yet for the case — the UI should show the
full picker in that case rather than nothing.

seq.title: Seq
seq.description: This item's monotonic position in the thread — the tie-break half of the paging cursor, sent back as `before_seq` alongside `before`. `null` for an upload bubble, which has no message row; the timestamp alone is a safe cursor there. Note this is a GLOBAL counter, not per-thread or per-tenant: consecutive items in one thread will not have consecutive `seq` values, and the gap reflects platform-wide write volume. That exposure is a knowing, accepted trade for a cursor that can address a row.

ThreadPage.title: ThreadPage
ThreadPage.description: A chronological page of party thread items.

TransactionRegion.title: TransactionRegion
TransactionRegion.description: A single parquet region (typically one page of a bank statement).

TransactionRow.title: TransactionRow
TransactionRow.description: One transaction row read from a parquet region.

UserInputFieldOptionResponse.title: UserInputFieldOptionResponse
UserInputFieldOptionResponse.description: One selectable option in an enum-style operator-adjustable input.

UserInputFieldResponse.title: UserInputFieldResponse
UserInputFieldResponse.description:
One operator-adjustable spec input declared by a policy spec.

Mirrors the YAML ``user_input:`` block: the host renders this as a
form field, validates the value against the declared constraints, and
POSTs the chosen value back under ``context[product_id].inputs.<name>``.

UserInputsGroupSectionResponse.title: UserInputsGroupSectionResponse
UserInputsGroupSectionResponse.description:
A shared override section for products that share a group declaration.

Emitted when one or more requested products opt into the same
``override_groups`` entry in ``loan_products.yaml``. The UI renders
a single section (e.g. "Qualified Mortgage" Y1/Y2 pickers) and the
host fans the operator's value out to ``context[product_id].inputs[...]``
for every product in ``applies_to_products``.

UserInputsProductSectionResponse.title: UserInputsProductSectionResponse
UserInputsProductSectionResponse.description:
Operator-adjustable fields scoped to one product (e.g. all FNMA knobs).

Excludes any field that came from a shared override group — those
are emitted ONCE in ``UserInputsSchemaResponse.groups`` instead, so
the UI doesn't render duplicate pickers across QM products in a
multi-product scenario.

UserInputsSchemaResponse.title: UserInputsSchemaResponse
UserInputsSchemaResponse.description:
Full operator-adjustable schema for a scenario/refinement.

Two-tier rendering surface:

  * ``groups``  — shared sections (one per active override group). A
    scenario picking all QM products renders a single "Qualified
    Mortgage" group with Y1/Y2 pickers.
  * ``products`` — per-product sections holding product-specific +
    spec-level overrides (group-sourced fields are stripped).

The host writes user-chosen values to
``context[product_id].inputs[<field_name>]`` regardless of which
section the field lives in. Group sections fan their writes out to
every product in ``applies_to_products``; product sections write
directly.
